idiom_name: MikroORM inheritance mapping (STI discriminatorMap, TPT inheritance: 'tpt')
implementation_notes: MikroORM declares the mapper structure rather than generating it implicitly: a base class used as a mapped superclass (not decorated as an entity) gives column reuse, discriminatorColumn plus discriminatorMap (or a discriminatorValue per child) gives single-table inheritance, and inheritance: 'tpt' on the root gives table-per-type, where the ORM inserts and joins each level automatically. The classic per-class mapper is therefore configuration; the remaining hand-written work is the domain logic, not the row mapping.
pitfalls: Decorators require experimentalDecorators/emitDecoratorMetadata in tsconfig; the defineEntity API avoids them but is the only option when the project is plain JavaScript.
A base class that must stay a mapped superclass is only non-entity by omission - decorating it by accident makes it queryable and changes the discriminator map.
TPT writes touch every table in the hierarchy per flush, so bulk mapper runs do one insert per level per object unless the ORM batches them.

variants.name: TypeORM single table inheritance (@TableInheritance/@ChildEntity)
variants.implementation_notes: TypeORM supports single table inheritance natively - @TableInheritance({ column }) on the root plus @ChildEntity() on each subclass, stored in one table with a discriminator - and concrete table inheritance by extending an abstract base class that is not itself an entity (each subclass gets its own table, columns duplicated). It has no joined/table-per-type mapping, so a class-table schema needs hand-written mappers or MikroORM.
pitfalls: Joined/table-per-type hierarchies are not expressible: trying to model them with @ChildEntity produces one wide table with nullable subclass columns.
Migrations from the entity metadata rewrite the single table when a subclass changes, so discriminator changes need a data migration.
Eager relations on child entities multiply queries because the discriminator filter is applied per entity type.
